channel.title: Blog on My Discombobulated Brain
channel.description: Recent content in Blog on My Discombobulated Brain

item.title: #RealPeople - Nicola
item.description: An honest personal story about postpartum psychosis, postnatal depression, severe depression, and mental health after childbirth. Explore the symptoms of postpartum psychosis, paranoia, anxiety, suicidal thoughts, diagnosis and treatment, and one mother’s journey towards recovery, motherhood, and rebuilding her confidence.

item.title: Jack Sargeant
item.description: Breaking the stigma around mental health starts with talking. This powerful story explores mental health support for men, the role of football and pubs in reaching people who may struggle to ask for help, and why conversations about mental health can remind us that no one is alone.

item.title: Newport County AFC and My Discombobulated Brain partnering to start the conversation
item.description: My Discombobulated Brain and Newport County AFC launch mental health drop-in sessions at Bar Amber in Newport, providing a safe space for fans and the community to talk about depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, and mental health. Find out how these sessions offer support, connection, education and signposting to mental health services.

item.title: #RealPeople - Anon
item.description: An honest personal story about depression, anxiety, self-harm, suicidal thoughts, and mental illness. Explore the reality of living with mental health problems, reaching a crisis point, psychiatric hospital treatment, and the journey towards mental health recovery, counselling, CBT, and breaking the stigma surrounding mental illness.

item.title: Say thank you
item.description: A medical student from Cardiff Medical School shares her personal experience of anxiety, anxiety attacks, emotional overwhelm, and mental health struggles. This honest story explores anxiety and guilt, feeling like a burden, emotional meltdowns, self-compassion, and learning to manage anxiety without constantly saying sorry.

item.title: Problem with open door policies
item.description: An honest personal story about depression, mental illness, and the challenges of asking for help. Explore mental health support, feeling like a burden, loneliness, depression, and the importance of talking openly about mental health. Discover why genuine support requires understanding, communication, and meaningful conversations about mental illness.

item.title: #RealPeople Alex
item.description: Alex shares his personal experience of depression, anxiety, suicidal thoughts, and mental health struggles at university. His honest depression recovery story explores antidepressant treatment, reaching a mental health crisis, seeking support, breaking mental health stigma, and discovering hope after feeling completely hopeless.

item.title: Dating with a mental illness
item.description: Dating with bipolar disorder and mental illness can bring anxiety, fear of rejection, and worries about stigma. This honest personal story explores relationships, dating with mental health problems, self-harm scars, bipolar disorder, vulnerability, mental health disclosure, and the fear of being judged.

item.title: A mentally challenging sport, with a mental health disorder
item.description: Explore the connection between competitive powerlifting and mental health in this honest personal story. Discover the challenges of training with a mental health disorder, including diagnosis, medication side effects, depression, anxiety, competition pressure, mental resilience, support, and learning to accept setbacks.

item.title: #RealPeople - Becky
item.description: Becky shares her honest mental health story, from childhood depression and anxiety to self-harm, alcohol, and risky behaviour. Her journey explores recovery, finding support, building resilience, and learning that life can get better, even after some of the darkest moments.

item.title: A Bipolar Christmas
item.description: Living with bipolar disorder at Christmas can bring depression, loneliness, anxiety, emotional overwhelm, and unpredictable moods. This honest personal story explores bipolar disorder, Christmas mental health, family pressure, and the importance of self-care, rest, and accepting that it’s okay not to be okay.

item.title: A true tale
item.description: An anonymous supporter shares their honest story of being diagnosed with bipolar disorder, challenging mental health stigma and misconceptions about bipolar disorder. They describe mood swings, depression, self-harm, medication, uncertainty, and the difficult journey towards acceptance, recovery, and learning healthier ways to cope with mental illness.

item.title: #RealPeople - Katie
item.description: An honest personal story about eating disorder recovery, mental illness, and the stigma surrounding eating disorders. Exploring anorexia, bulimia, distorted body image, secrecy, isolation, anxiety, and the impact of mental illness on relationships, work, and everyday life. A powerful reflection on seeking help, challenging mental health stigma, finding support and taking the first steps towards eating disorder recovery.

item.title: #RealPeople - Zoe
item.description: Zoe shares her real-life mental health story of eating disorders, including bulimia and EDNOS, alongside body image struggles, low self-esteem, anxiety and depression. Her honest recovery story explores abuse, body dysmorphia, eating disorder stigma, self-worth and finding strength through lived experience.

item.title: A Depression Survivor
item.description: Discover Nikki’s honest and personal mental health blog, sharing real experiences, thoughtful reflections and open conversations about life and mental health. Based in the USA, Nikki writes with honesty and authenticity, and here we highlight three of her blog posts that are well worth reading and adding to your regular reading list.

item.title: Staying strong as a network
item.description: Staying Strong as a Network explores how social media and online communities can provide mental health support, challenge mental health stigma, and help people connect with others. John Sennet shares how the web can create safe spaces to talk openly about mental health, share experiences, and realise you are not alone.

item.title: The Senedd and Leanne Wood
item.description: A visit to the Senedd in Cardiff and a meeting with Leanne Wood, former Plaid Cymru leader, to discuss mental health in Wales, mental health services, access to support, suicide prevention, mental health stigma, and improving care for people experiencing mental health difficulties.

item.title: Disasters with decision making?
item.description: Guest post by Ann from Rainbows Are Too Beautiful about raising a child with autism and ASD. Read her personal journey, her experiences of parenting a son with autism, and how she raises awareness and supports parents of children with autism and associated disorders.

item.title: #RealPeople - Steve
item.description: A deeply personal story about depression, grief, family mental health, and the stigma that can make asking for help feel impossible. Reflecting on loss, denial, isolation, and recovery, this powerful account explores the importance of family, friendship, therapy, and breaking the silence around mental health.

item.title: Whitchurch Hospital Exhibition
item.description: A visit to the Whitchurch Hospital exhibition before its closure became a deeply emotional experience. Walking the hospital corridors brought back memories of living with mental illness, while the exhibition revealed the history of mental health care in Cardiff, from its former patients and staff to changing attitudes and language around mental health. Discover why Dr Edwin Goodall became one of my mental health heroes.

item.title: #RealPeople - Coral
item.description: Coral got on board with our #SickNotSad campaign, and we started talking. It turns out that this lovely lady not only loves her coffee; she is an amazing blogger.
